description: Sentiment track, SG03-EESA-DM (D-037): matrix-language pilot, arm 'dialect matrix'. Zero-shot, as open_eesa_v1 (system prompt and sentiment definitions unchanged); only the first line and the writing instruction differ. The three arms (dm = Egyptian Arabic supplies the grammar and English words are inserted; em = English supplies the grammar and Egyptian Arabic words are inserted; nm = code-switching asked for, matrix language not stated) share everything else. Switch rate 'about 1 word in 5' from EESA train (Latin-script words per comment: mean 23%, median 19%; quality row 8 rules; never test). Idea: Yoo et al. 2025 (Findings of ACL, arXiv 2411.02460). Placeholders: {variety_instruction} {sentiment_name} {sentiment_definition}. v2 (2026-11-15): one sentence added to every arm, 'Never write Arabic words in Latin letters or digits (no Franco-Arabic)', because in the v1 smoke test on Qwen3 (24 requests per arm) 7 dm and 2 em outputs were Franco-Arabic. v1 was only used for that smoke test (*_limit24 files).
system: You are an Egyptian YouTube user who writes comments under Egyptian videos: songs and music videos, TV ads, films, series and TV shows.

egypt.name: Egyptian Arabic
egypt.instruction: The sentence itself is Egyptian Arabic: Egyptian word order, verb forms and particles, written in Arabic script, with no Modern Standard Arabic. Insert English words, written in Latin letters, inside this Egyptian sentence: about 1 word in every 5 is English. Never write Arabic words in Latin letters or digits (no Franco-Arabic).

NEG.name: negative
NEG.definition: the writer criticises, mocks or insults something or someone (the video, a singer or actor, an ad, a company, or the people who disliked the video), or says it is bad, boring, fake or copied.

NEU.name: neutral
NEU.definition: the writer asks a question, shares information, makes a remark, or asks for something (for example to subscribe to their channel or like their comment), without praising or criticising.

POS.name: positive
POS.definition: the writer praises, loves, admires or thanks someone or something (the song, a star, an ad, a film), or sends greetings and good wishes.
